card.hook: Here's the funny thing about Punta Nizuc: the point itself is mostly tucked behind a resort, so the best view is from the public beach next door. Pale sand, clear shallow water, a long horizon and almost nothing else in the way.
card.stand_here: Stand on the public beach at Playa Coral (El Mirador II) and use the phone icon on the map as your spot. Face the open water so the shoreline curves away towards the point.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the sand, sea and sky all in one go. Then try 1x for a cleaner, more natural look at the shoreline. If your phone has 2x or 5x, use it to pick out the point across the water.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the point or the water, then slide it a touch darker so the sky doesn't wash out and the water keeps its colour.
card.best_time: Go in the morning or late afternoon. The light is softer and the beach is more comfortable than at midday.
card.selfie_here: Try the Cancun sign, reached by walking along the beach past the beach clubs from the Punta Cancún area. Use the front camera at 0.5x and keep the sign over your shoulder. Check the exact spot on the map first, as the sign is listed at a few different addresses.
card.rules_and_safety: Don't try to reach the resort side or any private pier or pool, as those aren't public. Access can change, so check local access rules before you go.
card.challenge: Keep the horizon dead level and a strip of wet sand in the bottom of the frame. Bonus points if the curve of the beach leads straight to the point.
card.good_to_know: Punta Nizuc sits within the Parque Nacional Costa Occidental de Isla Mujeres, Punta Cancún y Punta Nizuc. Outside visitors may no longer be able to walk out to the tip itself. For a second photo with a different feel, go to the bridge at Puente Canal Nizuc and shoot across the channel, where the water leads your eye into the green.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the public beach at Playa Coral (El Mirador II) and use the phone icon on the map as your spot. Face the open water so the shoreline curves away towards the point.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found gives a spot where a passer-by should stand to frame the visitor with the whole Punta Nizuc landmark, so ask_someone_spot is null. The Cancun sign is listed under three different addresses (Punta Cancún/Punta Nizuc 210 on Evendo, and Punta Nizuc 335 on other pages), so check the exact location on a map before sending visitors. The Nizuc pool is inside a resort, and no page says whether non-guests may use it. Playa Delfines is called a photo spot on two pages (Flytographer, Hotels.com), but neither describes a selfie angle, so I left it out. No page states selfie stick or tripod rules; Evendo only suggests a tripod for group photos as a tip. A Pack Lightly page warns of strong currents at Punta Nizuc, but it describes a site in Guadalajara, so I did not use it as a safety point. Search budget ran out before I could verify the spots on a map.

card.hook: Big, colourful CANCÚN letters, a sea that looks almost too turquoise to be real, and a whole bay curving away behind them. This is the shot everyone comes to Playa Delfines for.
card.stand_here: Face the letters and the sea with the sun behind you. The letters may be at the beach entrance or beside the lookout, so check on the day exactly where they stand before you walk.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to fit the letters, the sea and the curve of the bay in together. Then try 2x for a tighter, more natural-looking frame.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and put the horizon on the top or bottom line so the sea stays straight and the bay's curve shows.
card.best_time: Aim for early morning, roughly 7:30 to 9:30, when the light comes from the side and the crowds are small. Queues build from mid-morning and the sign is busiest around midday, so come back at sunset if you want a colourful sky.
card.selfie_here: On the raised lookout at El Mirador, stand in front of the big CANCÚN letters, slightly to the left of the sign, so the ocean stays behind you. Use the front camera, and try 0.5x if you want more of the letters and sea in the shot.
card.rules_and_safety: Swimming currents are strong, so stay at the shoreline. Seaweed and strong surf can affect the beach from summer to autumn.
card.challenge: Get the horizon dead straight and the whole curve of the bay in the frame, with the letters sitting proudly in front. Bonus points for a shot with nobody's head in it.
card.good_to_know: Playa Delfines is on the Caribbean coast of Cancún, and El Mirador is its lookout platform. The CANCÚN letters are at or near the lookout. For a closer, head-on shot of just the letters with the ocean behind, try the Letrero CANCÚN viewpoint instead.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Go to the south end of the El Mirador lookout platform, about 66 m to the east of the phone icon, roughly 1 minute on foot. Face the letters and the sea with the sun behind you. The letters may be at the beach entrance or beside the lookout, so check on the day exactly where they stand before you walk.

selfie_research.notes: No page named a specific spot where a passer-by should photograph a visitor with the whole beach or landmark in frame, so ask_someone_spot is null. No page stated a rule about selfie sticks or tripods; one guide only suggests a mini tripod with timed selfie mode as a tip. Sources disagree on the location: one puts the beach at km 17, another at km 18, another at km 19.5, and one lists coordinates of 21.0785, -86.7712, about 2 km from the position you gave (21.06196, -86.77858). card.hook: Picture warm sand, a few palms leaning over calm bay water, and hardly anyone walking through your shot. That's the quiet western end of Playa Tortugas, and it's an easy place to take a good photo without trying very hard.
card.stand_here: Stand on the sand near the water at the western stretch of Playa Tortugas, away from the pier, right where the phone icon sits. Face the water so the waterline, the curve of the shore and the palms all fit in the frame.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to fit the waterline, shore and palms together. Switch to 0.5x if you want more sand, a rocky outcrop in the foreground and the wide bay.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the waterline on the lower or upper third, and crouch a little so some wet sand or a rock sits in the foreground.
card.best_time: Go late afternoon to sunset for soft, warm light on the sand and palms. The beach faces north, so don't expect a fiery sunset over the water. Think gentle golden glow instead.
card.selfie_here: Walk over to the wooden pier with its thatched roofs and put the turquoise water behind you. Use the front camera at 0.5x and hold your phone a little low so the pier fits over your shoulder. Guides say sunrise or sunset is when it's less crowded.
card.ask_someone: Ask someone to stand on the sand next to the ferry terminal beside the pier and frame you with the pier in the picture. No exact angle is known, so shuffle around until it looks good.
card.rules_and_safety: The pier is used for paid bungee and zipline activities, so check conditions locally if you plan to go on it. Check the currents before you go in the water. Vendors may come up to you on busy days, and a polite no and a short walk west is usually enough.
card.challenge: Find a palm that leads your eye along the shore, then add a rock or wet sand in the foreground and see if the photo suddenly feels deeper.
card.good_to_know: Playa Tortugas is on the calm bay side of Cancún, near the pier. From the pier you can see Isla Mujeres on the horizon. Seaweed (sargassum) can affect the shoreline on some days, so check the water before you choose your shot.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the sand near the water at the western stretch of Playa Tortugas, away from the pier, right where the phone icon sits. Face the water so the waterline, the curve of the shore and the palms all fit in the frame.

Pages disagree on the location pin: an Airial reviewer says the Google Maps pin is incorrect and to drive about 5 minutes further on, so check the spot on the ground. The Yelp listing spells it 'Playa Tortuga' and sits at Km 6.5 Boulevard Kukulcán, which is consistent with the coordinates.
